llm.summary: This is a disclosed Mistral AI connector that can read and change Mistral account data through OOMOL, with no evidence of hidden or malicious behavior.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is operating Mistral AI, and the documented actions all fit that purpose: chat, agents, conversations, embeddings, OCR, transcription, moderation, models, files, libraries, shares, and related lifecycle operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill routes broadly to Mistral AI for read, create, update, and delete tasks, but it scopes execution to the mistral_ai connector, requires live schema inspection before payload construction, and explicitly requires confirmation before write or destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It includes first-time setup instructions for installing the oo CLI with curl-to-shell or PowerShell and logging in only after a missing-command or auth failure; this is disclosed but should be treated as a privileged setup step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared tool access is limited to Bash(oo *), which is proportionate for an OOMOL connector skill; local inspection found only markdown action documentation and no hidden scripts, broad filesystem indexing, or unrelated network destinations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill requires an OOMOL-connected Mistral account and server-side credential injection, but it does not instruct credential harvesting, local token storage, background workers, startup persistence, or privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable connecting Mistral AI through OOMOL and letting the skill run oo connector actions on your behalf. Review exact payloads before uploads, sharing, updates, or deletes, and avoid exposing signed URLs, fileTransit download links, conversation history, or document text beyond the intended recipients.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad Mistral AI routing is real, but it is coherent with a service connector and is tempered by explicit confirmation requirements for create, update, send, post, delete, and remove operations.
[SQP-2] expected: The download and signed-link actions are expected for file and document retrieval. The docs disclose fileTransit and temporary signed URLs, but users should still treat returned links and file contents as sensitive.
[staticScan] expected: Static scan reported no suspicious patterns, and artifact review found markdown-only instructions plus connector command references.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean with no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this supports but does not determine the benign verdict.
